title: Biological Molecules and Enzymes
seo_title: Anatomy and Physiology 12: Biological Molecules and Enzymes Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Homeostasis is maintained through physiological processes: carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids, enzymes and metabolism, and membrane structure and transport. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Anatomy and Physiology 12)
meta_desc: Free Anatomy and Physiology 12 worksheets (BC Curriculum): biomolecules, enzymes and membrane transport. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Enzymes lower the activation energy of reactions.
body_html:
How to think about it

The four main biomolecules are carbohydrates (energy, made of sugars), lipids (energy storage and membranes), proteins (made of amino acids; enzymes, structure, transport) and nucleic acids (DNA and RNA, made of nucleotides). They are built by dehydration synthesis and broken by hydrolysis.

Enzymes are proteins that speed up metabolic reactions by lowering the activation energy. The substrate fits the active site; temperature, pH, and inhibitors affect the rate. The cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer that controls transport by diffusion, osmosis, facilitated diffusion and active transport.

Example

Which molecule is made of amino acids?

Enzymes are this type.

Answer: a protein

Example

How does a competitive inhibitor work?

It looks like the substrate.

Answer: it blocks the active site

Common mistakes

  • Thinking enzymes are used up.
  • Mixing up hydrolysis and dehydration synthesis.
  • Thinking active transport needs no energy.

items.q: How many peptide bonds are in a single polypeptide chain of 20 amino acids?
items.e: A chain of n amino acids has n − 1 peptide bonds: 19.

items.q: How many peptide bonds are in a single polypeptide chain of 3 amino acids?

items.q: Which bond joins two α-glucose molecules in maltose?
items.e: Formed by a condensation reaction.

items.q: What is the most abundant protein in animals?

items.q: What is the Michaelis constant K<sub>m</sub>?

items.q: Serine (M<sub>r</sub> 105) and alanine (M<sub>r</sub> 89) join to make a dipeptide. Calculate the M<sub>r</sub> of the dipeptide.

items.q: How many water molecules are released when 25 glucose molecules join to form a polysaccharide chain?

items.q: What bond joins nucleotides in a polynucleotide?

items.q: How many water molecules are released when 50 glucose molecules join to form a polysaccharide chain?

items.q: What is the secondary structure of a protein?

items.e: Hydrogen bonds between –NH and –C=O groups.

items.q: What is the most abundant protein in the whole biosphere?
items.e: It fixes CO₂ in photosynthesis.

items.q: How does a competitive inhibitor work?
c: it binds elsewhere and changes the active site shape

items.q: Why does a change in pH affect enzyme activity?

it binds away from the active site and changes its shape
it raises the activation energy only
items.e: More substrate does not reduce its effect.

items.q: In the DNA of a fungus, 15% of the bases are adenine. What percentage are cytosine?
items.e: A + T = 30%, so G + C = 70%, and cytosine = half of that: 35.0%.

items.q: A potato strip had a mass of 3.20 g. After 30 minutes in a solution its mass was 3.36 g. What is the percentage change in mass?
items.e: Percentage change = (final − initial) ÷ initial × 100 = 0.16 ÷ 3.20 × 100. Water entered by osmosis: the solution had a higher water potential.

items.q: A potato strip had a mass of 8.00 g. After 30 minutes in a solution its mass was 10.00 g. What is the percentage change in mass?
items.e: Percentage change = (final − initial) ÷ initial × 100 = 2.00 ÷ 8.00 × 100. Water entered by osmosis: the solution had a higher water potential.
